items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: I was in the Army with Cannonball, Cannonball and Nat.

ctx.x: Tell us, you did some work with the Adderleys.
Yeah. I was in the Army with Cannonball, Cannonball and Nat. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
First of all I got to say if I had to pick a quintet that just to me had a beautiful jazz feeling and a beautiful soul feeling it would be the Cannonball quintet.

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was in the Army with Cannonball... Cannonball was the head of the Band Training Unit.

ctx.x: Were there occasions where you’d have to say I don’t know that but tomorrow I will?

Yeah, yeah. Sometimes I’d learn it on the gig. Maybe I’d heard the tune but had never played it. They stuck pretty much to standards, plus most of them, you know I was great for listening to records in those days. Like in the Army, I was in the Army with Cannonball and we had more records than we had clothes in our barracks.
